'''Hormuud Telecom Somalia Inc.''' is a privately held [[telecommunications]] company based in [[Mogadishu]], [[Somalia]]. It is the largest telecommunication company and largest private-sector employer in the country, and also Somalia's first private enterprise to be internationally [[International Organization for Standardization|ISO]] certified.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Odero |first=Carol |date=August 21, 2021 |title=The Somali Phoenix That Is Hormuud Telecom |url=https://www.cioafrica.co/the-somali-phoenix-that-is-hormuud-telecom/ |publisher=[[CIO (magazine)|CIO]]}}</ref>

The company operates numerous services, including its mobile money transfer service.

The corporation is one of the only in Somalia to have a charitable arm, the Hormuud Salaam Foundation, which was launched in 2009. During the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Somalia|COVID-19 pandemic in the country]], Hormuud made numerous donations to the [[Healthcare in Somalia|Somali healthcare system]].

Hormuud launched 5G in Somalia in 2024.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Sridhar |first1=M.A. |last2=Paranjpe |first2=P. |chapter=An object-oriented framework for embedded WWW applications |date=1996 |title=Proceedings of COM'96. First Annual Conference on Emerging Technologies and Applications in Communications |chapter-url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1109/etacom.1996.502486 |publisher=IEEE Comput. Soc. Press |pages=97–100 |doi=10.1109/etacom.1996.502486|isbn=0-8186-7585-3 }}</ref>

==History==
Hormuud was established in 2002 in Mogadishu, Somalia by a small group of shareholders, and originally consisted of 16 telecommunication sites.<ref name="total" />

Ahmed Mohamed Yusuf, Hormuud Telecom's CEO joined Hormuud Telecom in 2002 with the intention to rebuild Somalia by connecting people with life-changing connectivity services. In the same year as its launch, Hormuud launched its fixed phone line service and [[GSM]], a second-generation digital mobile network, which became widely used in Europe and other parts of the world.<ref name="total" />

In 2011, the company conducted a mobile money transfer through EVC Plus, the first of its kind in Somalia. EVC Plus functions as a [[digital wallet]], allowing users to purchase goods and services and transfer money. Automated payments and [[SMS]] reminders were also added as features. Financial reports on EVC Plus can also be viewed without an [[Internet access|internet connection]].<ref name="Owuor 2018" /> In December 2012, Hormuud launched its Tri-Band [[3G]] service for mobile and internet clients. Also the first of its kind in the country, this 3G mobile telecommunications technology offers users a faster and more secure connection.<ref name="Sgtgms">{{Cite news |date=30 December 2012 |title=Somalia gets 3G mobile service |work=Shabelle Media Network |url=http://shabelle.net/somalia-gets-3g-mobile-service/ |url-status=usurped |access-date=23 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130108083430/http://shabelle.net/somalia-gets-3g-mobile-service/ |archive-date=8 January 2013}}</ref>

In July 2014, Hormuud Telecom, along with NationLink and [[Somtel]], signed an interconnection agreement. The cooperative deal established the [[Somali Telecommunication Company]] (STC), which allowed their mobile clients to communicate across all three networks.<ref name="Hsnsid">{{Cite news |date=23 July 2014 |title=Hormuud, Somtel, Nationlink sign interconnection deal |agency=TeleGeography |url=http://www.telegeography.com/products/commsupdate/articles/2014/07/23/hormuud-somtel-nationlink-sign-interconnection-deal/ |access-date=23 October 2014 |archive-date=1 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230501145409/https://www.telegeography.com/products/commsupdate/articles/2014/07/23/hormuud-somtel-nationlink-sign-interconnection-deal/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Later that year, Hormuud trialed the first 4G services in Somalia. They began expanding their 4G network capacity in 2015 in partnership with the [[Ministry of Telecommunications (Somalia)|Somalian Ministry of Telecommunications]].<ref name="hcygb" />

In 2009, Hormuud Telecom established the Hormuud Salaam Foundation, becoming the first corporate foundation in Somalia.{{citation needed|date=January 2022}} In 2019, the company offered commission-free bulk cash transfers to [[NGO]]s responding to floods around [[Beledweyne]], [[Baidoa]], [[Jowhar]], and the [[Gedo]] region of southern Somalia. This allowed the Somali Cash Consortium and other NGOs to provide direct donations to vulnerable Somalis in need.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 6, 2019 |title=Hormuud Telecom offers commission free transfers to NGOs responding to floods in Southern Somalia |url=https://reliefweb.int/report/somalia/hormuud-telecom-offers-commission-free-transfers-ngos-responding-floods-southern |publisher=ReliefWeb}}</ref>

In 2020, the company became the first private corporation in Somalia to be ISO certified. This international standard accredited Hormuud's products and services as satisfying the needs of their customers through an effective [[quality management system]] and meeting all the relevant regulatory requirements.<ref name="total" />

In 2021, Hormuud announced plans to guarantee nationwide [[4G]] coverage by 2023 in Somalia. It calculated that 30% of its 3.6 million customers still rely on 2G networks, the majority of whom reside in rural areas. The expansion will provide rural communities access to fast internet services, which is essential for both nationwide and rural [[economic development]]. Access to 4G is a major goal of Hormuud, in line with the [[United Nations]]' [[Sustainable Development Goals]] (SDGs).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tredger |first=Christopher |date=July 9, 2021 |title=Hormuud Telecom announces plan to expand 4G network |url=https://itweb.africa/content/nWJadvbeArRqbjO1 |publisher=ITWeb Africa}}</ref> In February 2021, the [[Central Bank of Somalia]] issued the first mobile money licence to Hormuud Telecom, assuring that its mobile money platform EVC Plus is now formally regulated and licensed by the Central Bank. The move formalised digital payments as a payment method within the country and will enable further integration of the Somali financial system with the international financial system.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 1, 2021 |title=Hormuud Telecom's mobile money first for Somalia |url=https://www.capacitymedia.com/articles/3827857/hormuud-telecoms-mobile-money-first-for-somalia |publisher=Capacity Media}}</ref>

Hormuud also launched Somalia's first indigenous mobile money app early in the same year. WAAFI combines mobile money, communication, entertainment, and payments, wherein consumers can access bank accounts, perform [[E-commerce|online transactions]], send international remittances, and make international/domestic phone calls all through the app. WAAFI's integrated mobile money experience is an upgrade from the existing [[Unstructured Supplementary Service Data|USSD]] technology that many Somalis use.<ref name="garowe">{{Cite web |date=September 2, 2021 |title=Somalia's first advanced mobile money app |url=https://www.garoweonline.com/en/news/somalia/waafi-somalia-s-first-advanced-mobile-money-tech-app |publisher=[[Garowe Online]]}}</ref>

In 2023, Hormuud Telecom hosted its Somali Success Stories conference, bringing together government leaders, industry representatives and over fifty businesses to celebrate the businesses and innovations driving Somalia's economic growth, and problem solve for the future.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-31 |title=Hormuud Telecom Convenes Somalia's Private Sector In Talks To Unlock Self-Sufficient Food Production - Africa.com |url=https://www.africa.com/hormuud-telecom-convenes-somalias-private-sector-in-talks-to-unlock-self-sufficient-food-production/ |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=www.africa.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2024, Hormuud Telecom's CEO Ahmed Yusuf was named CXO of the year at the Africa Tech Festival,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-06-30 |title=Hormuud Telecom's CEO, Ahmed Yusuf, Clinches CXO of the Year Award at Africa Tech Festival 2023 |url=https://www.garoweonline.com/en/news/somalia/hormuud-telecom-s-ceo-ahmed-yusuf-clinches-cxo-of-the-year-award-at-africa-tech-festival-2023 |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=Garowe Online |language=en}}</ref> and CEO of the year at the World Communications Awards.

In 2024, Hormuud Telecom brought 5G to Somalia, rolling out the service at no extra cost to customers in over 30 of Somalia's towns and cities. As a result of the first phase of the rollout 5G coverage in these areas stands at 81%.<ref name="Pham">{{Cite web |last=Pham |first=Manny |date=2024-03-21 |title=Hormuud launches 5G in Somalia |url=https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-business/operator-news/16448-hormuud-launches-5g-in-somalia.html |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=Developing Telecoms |language=en-gb}}</ref>

In partnership with [[Salaam Somali Bank]], Mastercard, Telesom, Golis and Paymentology, Hormuud Telecom introduced contactless payments in Somalia. Together, they launched a co-branded, tokenised, tap-to-pay digital companion card along with a physical card for Waafi mobile app users. The digital card is said to be a first for the [[Horn of Africa]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Grady |first=Vaughan |date=2024-08-06 |title=Salaam Bank and Paymentology target Somalia's Waafi mobile app users |url=https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-technology/financial-services/17119-salaam-bank-and-paymentology-target-somalia-s-waafi-mobile-app-users.html |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=Developing Telecoms |language=en-gb}}</ref>

The same year, Hormuud Telecom signed an MoU with the [[Federal Government of Somalia]]'s Ministry of Environment and Climate Change and Salaam Somali Bank to reinvest climate adaptation and mitigation funding into green initiatives within the country.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MSN |url=https://www.msn.com/en-xl/africa/top-stories/somalia-reaches-out-to-corporates-to-combat-climate-change/ar-BB1nO9VR?apiversion=v2&noservercache=1&domshim=1&renderwebcomponents=1&wcseo=1&batchservertelemetry=1&noservertelemetry=1 |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=www.msn.com}}</ref>

==Operations==
Hormuud Telecom has more than 3.6 million subscribers in Somalia, roughly three million of whom use its mobile money platform EVC Plus.<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Grady |first=Vaughan |date=March 1, 2021 |title=Could Somalia become the world's first cashless economy? |url=https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-technology/Clients/financial-services/Categories/10784-could-somalia-become-the-world-s-first-cashless-economy.html |publisher=Developing Telecoms}}</ref> More than 189,000 Somali investors have shares in Hormuud Telecom.<ref name="hcygb" />

Hormuud employs more than 20,000 full-time and part-time staff with different specialties,<ref name="Hiiraan Online">{{Cite web |title=Hormuud Telecom 'Creating jobs and improving lives' |url=http://www.hiiraan.com/op4/2020/feb/167144/hormuud_telecom_creating_jobs_and_improving_lives.aspx |access-date=2020-06-27 |website=Hiiraan Online}}</ref> including [[Telecommunications engineering|telecommunication engineering]], [[customer service]], sales and marketing, and finance specialists.<ref name="hcygb" /><ref>{{Cite press release |title=Hormuud Telecom Extends Microwave Backbone Through Addition of Harris Stratex Networks Technology |url=http://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/hormuud-telecom-extends-microwave-backbone-through-addition-of-harris-stratex-networks-technology-82675657.html |access-date=23 October 2014 |publisher=PR Newswire}}</ref> Around 45% of the firm's personnel are engineers.<ref name="hcygb" /> More than 17,999 Somali investors have shares in Hormuud Telecom.<ref name="hcygb">{{Cite web |last=Nyambura-Mwaura |first=Helen |date=2013-11-13 |title=Somalia's Hormuud rings up telecom profits despite anarchy |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-somalia-hormuud-idUKBRE9AC0WQ20131113 |access-date=2020-06-27 |website=U.S.}}</ref> It is the largest private employer in the country, with over 800 customer service centres in both urban and rural Somalia.<ref name="total" />

Hormuud provides a range of services for commercial, consumer, and residential use. They include fixed line services, GSM mobile services, 2G, 3G and 4G services, Hormuud [[MiFi|Mifi]], Enterprise Internet, and Hormuud [[Hotspot (Wi-Fi)|Hotspot]].<ref name="total" /> Hormud has no transport services. The company may rent bajajs (motorcycles) to drivers who pay a third of their earnings. As of 2021, the company operates predominantly in south and central Somalia and has 600 masts across the country.<ref name="total">{{Cite web |date=November 5, 2021 |title=20 years of driving connectivity in Somalia |url=https://www.totaltele.com/511579/20-years-of-driving-connectivity-in-Somalia |publisher=Total Telecom |access-date=January 21, 2022 |archive-date=November 5, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211105155222/https://www.totaltele.com/511579/20-years-of-driving-connectivity-in-Somalia |url-status=dead }}</ref>

As of 2021, it was estimated that over 11.25 million Somalis, or 70% of Somalia's population, have access to 4G internet.<ref name="hcygb" /> Hormuud also provides the cheapest 4G mobile [[internet in Africa]] and in the Arab world.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://technddigital.com/what-does-1gb-of-mobile-data-cost-in-every-country/ | title=What does 1GB of mobile data cost in every country? | date=2020-07-06 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200710031219/https://technddigital.com/what-does-1gb-of-mobile-data-cost-in-every-country/ | archive-date=2020-07-10 }}</ref> Hormuud Telecom has pledged to ensure full 4G coverage across Somalia by 2023.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mingas |first=Melanie |date=12 July 2021 |title=Hormuud Telecom sets out plan for nation-wide 4G coverage |work=Capacity Media |publisher=Capacity |url=https://www.capacitymedia.com/articles/3829086/hormuud-telecom-sets-out-plan-for-nation-wide-4g-coverage}}</ref>

== Technology and products ==
=== Mobile services ===
In 2002, Hormuud launched GSM Mobile Services, a prepaid service that offers options for contract or pay-as-you-go mobile services. Customers can top-up their accounts using Hormuud recharge vouchers and scratch cards.<ref name="total" />

In 2016, Hormuud launched its Ilwadaag service, which allows for [[Collect call|reverse calling]] and has become an important service for low-income Somalis. A whitelist was later added so that families and friends can connect more easily using the service.<ref name="total" />

=== Mobile internet and broadband ===
In 2013, Hormuud launched Hormuud Hotspot, a high-speed, secure, and reliable [[Wi-Fi]] [[Broadband Internet|broadband internet]] accessible in public places, hotels, and educational institutions.<ref name="total" /> In 2014, it launched Hormuud Mifi, a portable 4G wireless [[Router (computing)|router]] that can connect to multiple smartphones, tablets, or laptops and offers 4G internet for on-the-go web surfing. The same year, Hormuud launched ADSL Plus, a service that uses a customer's [[telephone line]] to send and receive internet data and make calls. At this time, internet capacity in the country was insufficient, yet subsequent capacity upgrades have allowed Hormuud to deliver high-speed fixed and home broadband services to households in Somalia.<ref name="total" />

Enterprise Internet, a broadband service that offers wireless internet services, was launched in 2014. It enabled simultaneous broadband connectivity sessions for multiple devices. The service is predominantly aimed at providing fixed broadband services for businesses and aid agencies working in Somalia.<ref name="total" /> During the same year, Hormuud also launched My SMS, a bulk messaging service for communication to a large workforce or group of students.<ref name="total" />

In 2024, Hormuud Telecom launched 5G services across Somalia, including Mogadishu, Kismayo, Galkayo, Baidoa, Dhusamareeb, Beledwayne, Afgoye, Merca, and Dhobley. 4G customers received upgrades to 5G at no extra cost, with 5G coverage in these areas reaching up to 81%. The 5G service offers speeds up to 400Gbit/s per wavelength, with total capacity options up to 38Tbit/s. Hormuud offers an unlimited data plan at $20 per month, one of the most affordable in Africa. Hormuud's 4G network, now covers 70% of Somalia's population, with a target of 88% urban and 70% rural coverage.<ref name="Pham"/>

In 2024, Hormuud Telecom signed up to the [[GSMA]]’s Humanitarian Connectivity Charter pledging to provide connectivity in times of crisis and enhance collaboration with humanitarian organisations. Hormuud Telecom has played a vital role in disaster response in Somalia by replacing basic ringtones with critical alert messages that provide public safety instructions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pham |first=Manny |date=2024-07-02 |title=Hormuud Telecom signs up to GSMA humanitarian charter |url=https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-business/operator-news/16943-hormuud-telecom-signs-up-to-gsma-humanitarian-charter.htmlhttps://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-business/operator-news/16943-hormuud-telecom-signs-up-to-gsma-humanitarian-charter.html |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=Developing Telecoms |language=en-gb}}</ref>

=== EVC Plus ===
First introduced in 2012, EVC Plus is a unique option to transfer and receive mobile money; it operates like SMS. Over 67% of Somalis, especially the most vulnerable communities, use mobile money technology as a sole payment system.<ref name="How We Made It In Africa 2020">{{Cite web |date=2020-03-02 |title=Meet the Boss: Ahmed Mohamed Yusuf, CEO, Hormuud Telecom (Somalia) |url=https://www.howwemadeitinafrica.com/meet-the-boss-ahmed-mohamed-yusuf-ceo-hormuud-telecom-somalia/64171/ |access-date=2020-06-27 |website=How We Made It In Africa}}</ref> EVC Plus differs from many other mobile money platforms in Africa by being totally free at the point of use. The mobile money platform has several key functionalities, such as person-to-person money transfer, person-to-merchant/business money transfer, airtime/data top-up, and account management.<ref name="Mohamed 2013">{{Cite web |last=Mohamed |first=Hamza |date=2013-08-31 |title=Electronic transfers improve Somalia economy |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/indepth/features/2013/08/2013831141614925682.html |access-date=2020-06-27 |website=Al Jazeera}}</ref>

Mobile money is widely used in Somalia, with data from the World Bank showing that mobile money transfer is crucial in Somali's economic and infrastructure growth, with 155 million transactions worth US$2.7 billion reported every month. The majority of these transactions are made through EVC Plus.<ref name="Owuor 2018">{{Cite web |last=Owuor |first=Victor Odundo |date=2018-10-12 |title=Somalia mobile money beats Kenya MPsea |url=https://qz.com/africa/1422018/somalia-mobile-money-beats-kenya-mpsea/ |access-date=2020-06-27 |website=Quartz Africa}}</ref> Research shows that mobile money plays a crucial role in minimising currency loss and [[Counterfeit money|fake money]].

[[Non-governmental organization|Non-governmental organisations]] (NGOs) and welfare organisations sending cash to Somalis in remote areas are exempted from the EVC wallet limit of $300. In the past, Hormuud Telecom provided commission-free bulk cash transfers to NGOs responding to crises (like floods in 2019).<ref name="ReliefWeb 2019">{{Cite web |date=2019-11-06 |title=Hormuud Telecom offers commission free transfers to NGOs responding to floods in Southern Somalia - Somalia |url=https://reliefweb.int/report/somalia/hormuud-telecom-offers-commission-free-transfers-ngos-responding-floods-southern |access-date=2020-06-27 |website=ReliefWeb}}</ref>

In 2019, Hormuud Telecom launched its humanitarian portal to better facilitate cash aid to remote and difficult to reach areas.<ref name="developingtelecoms.com">{{Cite web |last=Pham |first=Manny |date=2024-07-02 |title=Hormuud Telecom signs up to GSMA humanitarian charter |url=https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-business/operator-news/16943-hormuud-telecom-signs-up-to-gsma-humanitarian-charter.html |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=Developing Telecoms |language=en-gb}}</ref> The portal uses Hormuud's mobile money network to provide a traceable, timely and efficient way to distribute cash assistance – reducing risks and operating costs for NGOs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ngila |first=Faustine |date=2023-02-06 |title=This online platform eases cash aid transfers to rural Somalia |url=https://qz.com/new-platform-eases-cash-aid-transfers-to-rural-somalia-1850069213 |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=Quartz |language=en}}</ref> The portal can deliver aid to both feature phones and smartphones, and it is used by over 120 humanitarian partners.<ref name="developingtelecoms.com"/>

The portal won the Africa Tech Festival's Changing Lives award in 2022, for its role in transforming mobile money cash transfers and providing essential financial services to millions of Somalis during the 2021 drought.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-06-30 |title=Somalia: Hormuud Telecom Has Wins Yet Another International Award! |url=https://www.garoweonline.com/en/news/press-releases/somalia-hormuud-telecom-has-wins-yet-another-international-award |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=Garowe Online |language=en}}</ref>

In 2023, Hormuud Telecom partnered with the GSMA's GSMA Mobile for Humanitarian Innovation Programme (M4H) to increase the uptake of mobile-money enabled aid disbursement by INGOs. The goal of the partnership is to enable the exchange of [[best practice]], and spur innovation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barton |first=James |date=2023-06-14 |title=Hormuud Telecom and GSMA partner to drive INGO mobile money use |url=https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-technology/financial-services/15115-hormuud-telecom-and-gsma-partner-to-drive-ingo-mobile-money-use.html |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=Developing Telecoms |language=en-gb}}</ref>

In Somalia, 70.2% of mobile money users pay education fees on the platform; 56.4% disburse donations and charity; 28.3% shop online; 18.0% receive cash transfers from NGOs; and 16.7% pay government taxes.<ref name="Owuor 2018" /> Research from [[SIMAD University]] in [[Mogadishu]] has found that the adoption of mobile money throughout Somalia is responsible for the growth of small and medium-sized enterprises.{{Citation needed|date=April 2022}}

In 2024, Hormuud introduced interoperability in partnership with local banks, which enables seamless payments between bank accounts and mobile money wallets for the first time in Somalia. It allows EVC Plus customers to access basic banking functions like deposits and money transfers through the mobile money platform and means customers can make withdrawals without having to visit a physical bank.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pham |first=Manny |date=2024-10-18 |title=Hormuud bolsters mobile money platform with bank partnerships |url=https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-technology/financial-services/17487-hormuud-bolsters-mobile-money-platform-with-bank-partnerships.html |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=Developing Telecoms |language=en-gb}}</ref>

=== Nasiye ===
Nasiye was first launched in 2013, and became more prominent during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. This service allows a user to set up music or reading options as their dial tone. During the pandemic, Hormuud replaced some of the Nasiye dial tones with [[public health]] announcements to educate vulnerable populations and communities. Hormuud removed service subscription fees to help support the country from 2019 onwards.<ref name="total" />

=== WAAFI ===
In 2021, Hormuud launched Somalia's first indigenous mobile money application, which gives Somalis access to a range of digital services across a singular platform for the first time. On the WAAFI app, consumers can access [[bank account]]s, perform online transactions, send international remittances, and make international and domestic phone calls.<ref name="waafi">{{Cite web |date=April 22, 2021 |title=MOBILE FINANCE Hormuud Telecom launches Somalia's first mobile money app |url=https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-technology/financial-services/11013-hormuud-telecom-launches-somalia-s-first-mobile-money-application.html |publisher=Developing Telecoms}}</ref>

WAAFI is a fully integrated mobile money platform, upgrading existing USSD technology that many Somalis use. Currently, USSD-enabled mobile money technology has a penetration rate as high as 80% in urban areas and 55% in rural areas. WAAFI allows users to access their bank account through deposits and withdrawals via their EVC Plus wallet. Through this, businesses can generate QR codes that allow customers to directly credit the businesses' bank accounts.<ref name="waafi" />

In 2022, WAAFI won the Changing Lives Award, at the GSMA's GLOMO award ceremony for its role supporting in humanitarian situations.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The 2022 GLOMO Award Winners |url=https://www.mwcbarcelona.com/mobile-awards/2022-glomo-award-winners |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=MWC Barcelona |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In 2024, Hormuud's collaborated with WAAFI, Paymentology, Mastercard and Salaam Somali Bank to roll out “Tap and Go” contactless payments in Somalia for the first time. The WAAFI mobile app now allow users to digitally open an account, create a digital Mastercard card, attach the card to a wallet or account, tokenise the card on a digital device, so contactless payments can be conducted with ease.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Khoza |first=Lezeth |date=2024-08-02 |title=Paymentology partners Salaam Bank's Waafi mobile app |url=https://itweb.africa/content/KzQenMjy5ZY7Zd2r |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=ITWeb Africa |language=en-ZA}}</ref>

==Sponsorship==
In April 2019, the Hormuud Scholarship was launched, giving well-qualified Somali students full ride [[scholarship]]s to Somali universities.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Realizing the Dreams of Brilliant Students Through Hormuud's Scholarship |date=30 June 2020 |url=https://www.garoweonline.com/en/news/somalia/realizing-the-dreams-of-brilliant-students-through-hormuud-s-scholarship-program |publisher=[[Garowe Online]]}}</ref> Since 2015, Hormuud has also sponsored a number of regional and national [[book fair]]s across the country.<ref name="bookfair" />

Since 2005, Hormuud has sponsored the Banaadir Regional football league.<ref name="bookfair">{{Cite web |title=Hormuud supporting Literature and Learning, as 6th annual Mogadishu Book Fair Concludes |date=30 June 2020 |url=https://www.garoweonline.com/en/news/press-releases/hormuud-proud-to-support-literature-and-learning-as-the-6th-annual-mogadishu-international-book-fair-concludes |publisher=[[Garowe Online]]}}</ref> From 2013, it has also sponsored the annual [[Somalia Super Cup]], the domestic football league final.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Somalia launches regional league as national plan takes shape |url=https://hiiraan.com/news4/2017/Jan/139681/somalia_launches_regional_league_as_national_plan_takes_shape.aspx |publisher=[[Hiiraan Online]]}}</ref>

== Hormuud Salam Foundation ==
Hormuud Salam Foundation (HSF) is a non-profit foundation that is fully funded by Hormuud Telecom and Salaam Somali Bank, created for the sole purpose of providing charitable contributions to improving the everyday lives of Somalis.

In 2020, during the coronavirus pandemic, HSF and partners donated over US$5 million towards Somalia's coronavirus healthcare and pandemic relief efforts. In 2021, HSF supported the effort to help raise $4 million for the Somalia Action Network COVID-19 relief fund, in partnership with the Somali Chamber of Commerce.<ref name="garowe" />

In the same year, the HSF donated Somalia's first public [[oxygen plant]]. The plant, purchased from Turkey, was donated to help Somalia cope with severe shortages of medical oxygen. The plant was installed at the [[Banadir Hospital|Banadir Maternity and Children Hospital]], where the foundation has also funded the repair of its COVID-19 ward and the oxygen plant's storeroom.<ref name="hiiraan">{{Cite web |title=Hormuud Salaam Foundation donates $200,000 for Las Anod evictees |url=https://www.hiiraan.com/news4/2021/Oct/184221/hormuud_salaam_foundation_donates_200_000_for_las_anod_evictees.aspx |publisher=Hiiraan}}</ref>

HSF funds a range of philanthropic relief projects, directly responding to [[humanitarian crisis]] across Somalia.<ref name="hiiraan" />

In the winter of 2023, following ‘once in a century’ flooding in the region, Hormuud Salaam Foundation donated and distributed $1million in flood relief.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-06-30 |title=Amid raging floods, Hormuud Salaam Foundation donates $1 million to victims |url=https://www.garoweonline.com/en/news/somalia/amid-raging-floods-hormuud-salaam-foundation-donates-1-million-to-victims |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=Garowe Online |language=en}}</ref> The same year, Hormuud Salaam Foundation sponsored a year of fuel costs for the Banadir Maternity and Children's Hospital in Mogadishu, ensuring the uninterrupted running of services. The foundation also donated ten incubators.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-06-30 |title=Hormuud Salaam Foundation Pledges to pay for 2nd year fuel cost in Banadir Hospital |url=https://www.garoweonline.com/en/news/somalia/hormuud-salaam-foundation-pledges-to-pay-for-2nd-year-fuel-cost-in-banadir-hospital |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=Garowe Online |language=en}}</ref>

Hormuud Salaam Foundation also sponsored heart disease screening for 119 children in Mogadishu, led by Italian doctors Dr Marianeschi Stefano and Dr Scansani Silvia. As a result of the medial evaluations, 15 children have since been sent to Italy for life-saving surgeries, funded by HSF.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-12-04 |title=Hormuud Salaam Foundation Sponsors Vital Health Screening For Children With Heart Disease In Mogadishu - Africa.com |url=https://www.africa.com/hormuud-salaam-foundation-sponsors-vital-health-screening-for-children-with-heart-disease-in-mogadishu/ |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=www.africa.com |language=en-US}}</ref>
